title: Growth trends of common space complexity classes
summary: Compare how five space complexity classes grow as input size increases.
context: The horizontal axis shows input size n with ticks from 1 to 14; the vertical axis shows memory usage with no numeric capacity ticks. This schematic compares asymptotic growth trends rather than exact byte counts or unscaled function values.
description: The table below orders the five curves from lowest to highest at the right edge of the plot, matching the upward arrow on the right labeled "Lower → higher; better → worse".

frames.title: Growth trends of common space complexity classes
frames.explanation: At small sizes some schematic curves cross—for instance, between ticks 2 and 6 the logarithmic curve sits slightly above the linear line. What the plot conveys is the growth trend for sufficiently large n: constant stays flat, logarithmic grows slowly, and exponential eventually grows fastest; early crossings cannot be used to read off exact memory usage for specific inputs.

tables.caption: Five space complexity classes and curve shapes
headers: Complexity (low to high at right edge)
rows: Green horizontal line just above the horizontal axis, unchanged as n grows
Cyan curve rising slowly with gradually flattening slope
Blue straight line rising at a constant slope
Orange curve bending upward with increasingly steep slope
Red curve staying near the bottom around ticks 1 to 8 before shooting upward steeply
